title: Asymmetric HfO2/SiO2 20-layer stack with perturbed inner layers
scientific_hypothesis: Breaking the quasi-quarter-wave symmetry in layers 6-14 by ±6 nm perturbation will enable the gradient optimizer to escape the current local optimum attractor and discover alternative interference pathways that improve the target score beyond 0.1965.
design_principle: Spatial asymmetry initialization disrupts symmetric interference patterns that may trap gradient-based optimizers in suboptimal solutions. Outer layers (1-5 and 15-20) remain fixed to preserve boundary matching conditions while inner cavity region explores alternative phase relationships.
proposed_topology: exactly 20 finite layers from the incident side: HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Maximum 30 layers constraint satisfied with 20 layers
HfO2 and SiO2 are conventional depositable inorganic dielectrics
Thickness tolerance analysis not required for this optimization round
theory_basis: Symmetry-breaking in optimization landscapes to escape local minima
Quarter-wave stack theory for bandpass filter design
expected_advantages: May discover higher-performing thickness combinations unreachable from symmetric initialization
Maintains proven material pair from round 1 (0.5036 score)
Isolates asymmetry as the single variable change from prior iterations
known_risks: Asymmetry may degrade rather than improve performance if symmetric solution was near-optimal
Gradient optimizer may still converge to similar local optimum despite perturbation
HfO2 may exhibit absorption or surface quality issues at 255 nm per evidence
execution_request_english: Perform one bounded TMM thickness optimization for an exactly 20-layer planar stack. Use the fixed material sequence from the incident side: HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2. Optimize only the physical thickness of each finite layer within the user-declared bounds. Do not optimize material identity or layer count in this route. Optimize a 20-layer dielectric stack on fused silica substrate under air incidence. Material sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (20 finite layers total). Initialize layer thicknesses from the round 3 optimum candidate (thicknesses_nm: [35.09, 47.65, 35.10, 47.62, 35.10, 47.59, 35.06, 47.53, 34.97, 47.56, 34.95, 47.56, 35.07, 47.62, 35.07, 47.65, 35.08, 47.62, 35.07, 42.69]) but apply random perturbation of ±6 nm to layers 6 through 14 only (indices 5-13 in zero-based counting). Hold layers 1-5 and 15-20 at their round 3 optimum values during initialization. Perform bounded gradient-based thickness optimization with per-layer bounds of ±15 nm from initialized values. Spectral objectives: maximize mean transmittance 255-280 nm, minimize mean transmittance 300-700 nm, minimize mean transmittance 700-1100 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. No metal layers. Fused silica substrate. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 255–280 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Transmittance in 300–700 nm; Transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers; No metal layers; Only conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Following feedback directive to inject deliberate spatial asymmetry into layers 6-14 by ±6 nm perturbation from round 3 optimum while holding outer pairs fixed. This tests whether symmetry-breaking escapes the local optimization attractor that caused score regression from 0.5036 to 0.1965.
